summary: Backend-only testing of certificate XML sync (iteration_19 follow-up to iteration_18 party sync). Added test-scoped BouncyCastle to cpa-service pom, wrote CpaCertificateXmlParserTest (18 tests, real self-signed X.509 via BouncyCastle) and CpaServiceCertificateSyncTest (7 Mockito tests covering add/update-in-place/remove + 'XML wins over manual upload' rule on both create() and update()). All 58 unit tests pass (25 new + 33 existing regression: CpaPartyXmlParserTest 12, CpaServicePartySyncTest 5, CpaServiceUpdateTest 10, CpaControllerUpdateTest 6). Main agent's assumption confirmed: Mockito's default empty-list return for unstubbed certRepository.findByCpaId() and partyXmlParser.parseCertificates() does NOT NPE or break strict-stubbing in the existing tests. `mvn compile` and `mvn test-compile` succeed cleanly with no warnings introduced.

minor.issue: Testcontainers integration test errors with 'Could not find a valid Docker environment' - PRE-EXISTING, unrelated to this change (no Docker in the preview container). Not a code defect.

critical_code_review_comments: CpaPartyXmlParser.parseCertificates() correctly uses XXE-safe parseDocument(), namespace-agnostic getElementsByTagNameNS('*',...), strips whitespace from base64 via replaceAll('\\s+', ''), and parses validFrom/validUntil from the real X.509 (not from XML). Garbage base64 and empty X509Certificate are safely skipped with warn-log rather than thrown. Good.

CpaService.syncCertificates() reconciliation uses natural key (partyId + '::' + alias). Update-in-place preserves the same DB row (PK) which is essential to keep FK relationships intact. XML-wins rule works symmetrically on both create() and update() as user requested.

Minor consideration (not a bug): guessUsage() will classify an alias like 'design-certificate' as SIGNING because 'sign' is a substring. Consider word-boundary matching if false positives ever surface, but the current heuristic matches the spec ('contains sign/encrypt case-insensitively').
CpaService now has 6 collaborators via constructor - still acceptable. If it grows further consider splitting party-sync and cert-sync into a dedicated CpaXmlSyncService.

Test scope: CpaServiceCertificateSyncTest exercises the reconciliation orchestration; the DB uniqueness constraint (cpa_id, party_id, certificate_alias) is not exercised at the JPA level here - covered by the existing SpringBootTest integration test (skipped due to missing Docker).

success_rate.backend: 100% (58/58 unit tests; 1 pre-existing Testcontainers integration test skipped due to no-Docker env)

seed_data_creation: None (self-signed X.509 certs generated in-memory per test class via BouncyCastle helper).
context_for_next_testing_agent: cpa-service now has BouncyCastle at test scope (bcprov/bcpkix-jdk18on). CpaService constructor takes 6 collaborators: cpaRepository, partyRepository, channelRepository, certRepository, cpaMapper, partyXmlParser. syncCertificates() is unconditionally called after cpaRepository.save() in both create() and update(). Full regression suite for cpa-service (excluding the Docker-dependent CpaServiceIntegrationTest) is green under JDK 21.0.2 at /tmp/jdk-21.0.2 + Maven 3.9.9 at /tmp/apache-maven-3.9.9.
